correctness.rationale: For 1<p<∞ and any finite branching numbers b_j≥1, the level means A_j(M^k f)≤A_(j+k)(f) follow from each depth-k descendant occurring exactly once with equal weight. The scalar backward shift on Ces_p has sharp norm^p ζ(p)/ζ(p,k+1), derived by comparing increasing prefix sums u_n^p with strictly decreasing factors ((n+k+1)/(n+1))^p via the negative covariance identity; equality forces a single nonzero input at index k. Level-k functions with common nonzero complex phase attain the tree equality at the root; phase variation makes the triangle inequality strict. The Hurwitz-zeta tail integral test proves the stated k^(1−1/p) growth and r(M)=1. Independent p=2 tests exercised 2,500 finite sequences and all ten power spikes; not an infinite proof.
